description: n512 PAF kernel (qr_panel_apply_fused, 51%) is OCCUPANCY/BARRIER-bound per ncu: CTA-barrier stalls 34-39%, only ~2 CTA/SM (96KB SMEM), tensor pipe ~45% idle, NOT MMA-bound. Raise occupancy and cut barrier stalls: shrink the 96KB SMEM footprint (smaller staged tiles / drop redundant SMEM buffers / reuse) to fit 3-5 CTA/SM so the scheduler hides barrier latency, and reduce the number of __syncthreads per outer block (fuse phases, double-buffer, or async-copy pipeline so fewer full-CTA barriers). Goal: more concurrent CTAs to overlap the barrier-stall bubbles, attacking the 51% kernel at its real bottleneck.

Reverts the remote-invalid brief-4 BF16x9 bad-subset change (g_prec_emul/OB128-IB64/nlev=3); branch differs from clean baseline ONLY by the numerically-identical PAF carveout. Geomean 1638.8us vs clean-baseline 1635.2us (within noise). ncu: carveout lifts PAF SMEM block-limit 5->6 but Block Limit Registers stays 5 (48 regs) so achieved occupancy unchanged (51%, 0.86 waves at B=640/148SMs). n512 factor residual unchanged (scaled_factor_residual=0.00854, factor_rtol=0.00122). Numerically safe.

DELIVERABLE: commit 2264a71f6 = CLEAN baseline 769f6f8b9 + PAF carveout=MaxShared ONLY (brief-4 remote-invalid BF16x9 bad-subset change fully reverted; g_prec_emul=0). Geomean 1638us vs clean-baseline 1635us (re-measured 1638/1638/1638 -- WITHIN NOISE, numerically identical: n512 scaled_factor_residual=0.00854, factor_rtol=0.00122, byte-identical to clean PAF). Remote-valid (keeps baseline torch.geqrf bad-subset routing).

KEY FINDING -- the brief premise (96KB SMEM, 2 CTA/SM) is STALE by ~3x. Ground-truth ncu of the n512 PAF (qr_panel_apply_fused<8,1>, the 51% kernel, m_i=512 instance): SMEM=32.9KB (prior no_csh+no_vsh work already shrank it), 48 regs, Block Limit Registers=5 AND Block Limit Shared Mem=5 (a TIE), theoretical occ 62.5%, ACHIEVED 51%, Waves/SM=0.86. The grid is SUB-ONE-WAVE: B=640 CTAs / 148 SMs = 4.3 CTA/SM < the 5 the block-limit allows. So the kernel is WORK-STARVED at the SM level during barrier bubbles, NOT SMEM-limited. Memory is the higher SOL term (58% vs 45% compute); barrier stall 30-39% of issue interval (confirmed), from panel-phase warp DIVERGENCE (warp0 serial next-pivot vs depleting bulk-warp trailing work), not occupancy.

LEVERS TRIED (all on this kernel, measured): (t1) carveout=MaxShared -> SMEM block-limit 5->6 but regs still cap at 5 => NEUTRAL, numerically identical [KEPT as deliverable]. (t2) launch_bounds MINB=6 -> regs 48->40, 6-block-capable, but achieved warps stayed 8.2 (grid-bound) and panel chain recompute => 1637us, shape3 +3% SLOWER. (t3) no_vsh=0 (V in persistent smem, drop global Vg round-trip) -> 1630us, slightly slower (SMEM up -> fewer blocks; the prior +1% still holds). (t4) dense IB 16->32 (4x fewer/wider PAF launches, ~42% fewer barriers) -> 1719us MUCH slower: the 32-col serial panel latency + doubled SMEM (64KB->3 blocks) dominated.

CONCLUSION the occupancy/barrier-count levers inside the existing PAF kernel are spent: every edit that raises the block limit is neutralized by the 0.86-wave grid, and every edit that touches register pressure or panel width LENGTHENS the binding serial-panel critical path and regresses.

OPEN STRUCTURAL DIRECTIONS (need fresh briefs, larger scope, numerical care): (A) 2-MATRICES-PER-CTA with NAMED barriers -- pack 2 independent matrices/CTA (4 warps each, separate __barrier_sync ids) so matrix-B's warps issue while matrix-A's wait at its barrier; directly fixes the work-starvation/no-eligible-warp 48% the ncu flags. Doubles the grid to 1.7 waves. Risk: named-barrier reassociation could shift the panel reduction order (residual). (B) SPLIT THE APPLY (A6 C-=VY, 96 row-tiles, embarrassingly parallel) across 2 CTAs/matrix while keeping the panel on 1 CTA -> more CTAs/SM for the apply half. (C) ACTUAL source register reduction (not launch_bounds) to free the 6th block WITHOUT panel recompute -- but only pays if (A)/(B) first lift the grid above one wave. (D) attack the 58% MEMORY side: under no_csh the apply reads C from global twice (A4 V^TC, A6 C-=VY); a cp.async double-buffer of the C tiles would cut Long-Scoreboard stalls (numerically identical) but needs SMEM the budget lacks unless paired with a panel-SMEM cut. The dominant cost is the LATENCY-BOUND serial panel chain feeding a work-starved single-wave grid -- the highest-value attack is (A).

Dir-A 2-matrices-per-CTA PAF (named per-matrix barriers, 16 warps/CTA). New qr_panel_apply_fused_2mat_kernel, gated g_paf_2mat on the n512 8-warp path. Per-matrix math BIT-IDENTICAL: n512 scaled_factor_residual=0.00854/factor_rtol=0.00122 (byte-identical to clean, no cross-matrix contamination). REGRESSED: geomean 1680.8us vs clean 1635; shape3 3154->3977 (+26%). ncu: 64 regs (2 blocks/SM), SMEM 65.8KB, 1.08 waves but No-Eligible 53% (worse than 1-mat 48%), 174us/instance vs 122us. Decoupled barriers + bigger CTAs cut occupancy below the gain.

Geomean 1659.7us vs clean 1635 (still +1.5%); shape3 3559 (vs 3977 at t6, vs 3154 clean). ncu: 40 regs, SMEM 65.8KB, 0.72 waves (WORSE than 1-mat 0.86), No-Eligible 51%, 152us/instance. n512 residual bit-identical 0.00854. 2-mat reorganizes the same ~48 warps into bigger CTAs -- does NOT add the total warps the sub-one-wave SM needs; named barriers cost more than __syncthreads. Direction-A regresses as built.

DIRECTION-A (2-matrices-per-CTA) BUILT, VALIDATED, PROFILED, MEASURED -- it REGRESSES. KEEPER unchanged: HEAD f5326cd4 = clean baseline 769f6f8b9 + PAF carveout=MaxShared (1638us, n512 residual byte-identical 0.00854, g_prec_emul=0, +11 lines vs clean baseline).

Built qr_panel_apply_fused_2mat_kernel: 16 warps/CTA, 2 matrices, EACH on its own named barrier (bar.sync id g+1, count 256), disjoint per-group smem (gbase=smem+g*per_group_floats*4) and global (mat=blockIdx.x*2+g), group-local warp/tid used exactly where the 1-mat used warp/tid. NUMERICALLY PERFECT per the manager guard: n512 scaled_factor_residual=0.00854 / factor_rtol=0.00122 BYTE-IDENTICAL to clean across all validate runs -> zero cross-matrix contamination, no reduction reassociated.

BUT it regresses: (t6) g_paf_2mat=1 -> 1680.8us, shape3 3154->3977 (+26%). ncu: 64 regs -> 2 blocks/SM, SMEM 65.8KB, No-Eligible 53% (WORSE than 1-mat 48%), 174us/instance (vs 122). (t7) +launch_bounds MINB=3 -> regs 40, 3 blocks/SM, 1659.7us, shape3 3559 (still +13%); ncu 0.72 waves (WORSE than 1-mat 0.86), No-Eligible 51%, 152us/instance.

WHY DIR-A FAILS (root cause, measured): packing 2 matrices into one CTA does NOT add total warps to the SM -- it reorganizes the same ~40-48 warps into 2x-bigger CTAs, which (a) DOUBLES SMEM to 65.8KB -> fewer CTAs/SM -> 0.72 waves (below the 1-mat 0.86), (b) needs 64 regs (group-index arithmetic + larger live set) -> 2 blocks/SM unless throttled, and (c) the per-matrix NAMED barriers (bar.sync id,256) are MORE EXPENSIVE than the 1-mat's __syncthreads (bar.sync 0). The decoupling theory (sibling issues through the bubble) is real but the two groups SHARE the SM schedulers, so decoupling does not create new eligible warps -- it just splits existing ones -- while the occupancy/SMEM/barrier costs dominate. No-Eligible went UP, not down. The sub-one-wave deficit needs MORE CTAs (more total warps), and 2-mat makes FEWER, bigger CTAs.

WHAT'S STILL OPEN (these ADD total warps / CTAs, unlike 2-mat): (B) SPLIT THE APPLY across 2 CTAs/matrix -- the A6 C-=VY (96 parallel row-tiles) and A2/A4 are embarrassingly parallel; run the panel on 1 CTA, then a SECOND grid of 2*B CTAs for the wide apply. This genuinely DOUBLES apply-phase CTAs (more total warps), at the cost of unfusing (separate launch, re-stage V from the smem/global it already wrote). Likely the real win since the apply (not panel) carries the WMMA + the 58% memory. (C) PERSISTENT-CTA grid: launch exactly waves*148 CTAs, each looping over a strided set of matrices -- keeps the same per-matrix kernel but lets the scheduler overlap matrix k+1's panel-load with matrix k's apply tail WITHIN a CTA (no barrier coupling since they're sequential), turning the 0.86-wave tail into hidden latency. (D) cp.async double-buffer the global C reads (58% mem SOL), numerically identical, needs a paired panel-smem cut. The 2-mat result rules out 'bigger CTAs'; the path forward is 'more/persistent CTAs' (B/C). I recommend a fresh brief for (B) -- it is a larger unfuse+split restructure beyond tweaking the existing PAF kernel.

Shows FUSION is worth ~13% on the dominant shape (not ~0.5%) -- so direction B (unfuse + custom split-apply) starts from a 13% hole the extra-CTA wave gain must beat. n512 residual unchanged (cuBLAS apply is the FP32-V path).

So A6 is only ~14% of PAF (122-105=17us); panel+prep is ~86% and is SERIAL/unsplittable. The unfused A6 (47us, reads V/Y from global) costs MORE than the in-fusion A6 (17us). A6-split grid 1280 CTAs but Waves still 0.72, No-Eligible 52% -- A6 too short+memory-bound for extra CTAs to help. Manager premise 'apply is where the time is' DISPROVEN: the time is in the serial panel/prep, not the splittable A6.

WHY DIR-B FAILS (ncu, decisive): the fused PAF is 122us; PAF-prep (panel + S/M/W/Y, A6 removed) is 105us; A6-split is 47us -> 152us total (>122 fused). So (1) A6 is only ~14% of the PAF (122-105=17us in-fusion); the panel + S/M/W/Y prep is ~86% and the PANEL is SERIAL/unsplittable. (2) The unfused A6 costs 47us (reads V from global Vg + Y from global, vs resident SMEM in fusion) -- MORE than the 17us it cost inside fusion. (3) The A6-split grid is 1280 CTAs but still only 0.72 waves, No-Eligible 52% -- A6 is too short + memory-bound (1.01 TB/s, RMW on C) for extra CTAs to help. The manager premise 'the apply phase is where the time is' is DISPROVEN: the time is in the serial panel/prep (86%), not the splittable A6 (14%).

CUMULATIVE BRIEF-7 FINDINGS (all measured): the n512 PAF (51% of shape3) is SERIAL-PANEL-BOUND and SUB-ONE-WAVE (0.86), and EVERY occupancy/barrier/split lever the brief names has been built and regresses or is neutral: carveout (neutral, SMEM-limit 5->6 but regs cap 5) [KEEPER]; MINB reg-throttle (+3% slower, panel recompute); no_vsh=0 (slightly slower); IB 16->32 (+6%, wider serial panel); 2-mat/named-barriers dir A (+1.5-3%, bigger CTAs cut occupancy, don't add warps); unfuse-to-cuBLAS probe (+13%); split-A6 dir B (+13%, A6 only 14% + unfuse cost). 

ROOT CAUSE: the binding cost is the SERIAL Householder panel chain at m_i=512 (86% of PAF, 16 columns x O(m) m-passes with a per-column __syncthreads), feeding a sub-one-wave grid. Occupancy is grid-bound and the splittable work (A6) is small. 

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN (attacks the SERIAL PANEL, not occupancy -- needs fresh briefs): (1) SHORTEN the panel critical path itself -- e.g. recursive/blocked panel (split w=16 into 2x w=8 with a tiny trailing update) so the per-column serial chain halves; or a fundamentally different panel factorization (Cholesky-QR2 on the n512 good subset, which is GEMM-only/no serial Householder panel -- orthogonal to brief-5's tcgen05 panel work). (2) cp.async double-buffer the panel's per-column smem loads to cut the per-column barrier latency (another worker's lane). (3) accept that n512 PAF is near its architectural floor for the blocked-Householder algorithm and pivot the geomean attack to other shapes. I recommend the manager treat the n512 PAF occupancy/barrier/split space as measured-exhausted and redirect to PANEL-ALGORITHM change (Cholesky-QR2 good-subset) or other shapes.
